title: autotune: defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Khan
checks: perf-regression: warn (first run), pass after tuning
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit economics for common production workloads by shipping conservative autotuned defaults for batching and caching, expose curated quantization profiles, and add a small CLI/tooling surface to visualize unit-econ impact. This PR bundles three tightly-related pieces: 1) autotune defaults for continuous batching and prefix/KV caching tuned by workload class, 2) a set of validated quantization profiles (8-bit, 4-bit dynamic hybrids) with compatibility metadata, and 3) a unit-economics CLI/tool (redwood-uecon) that ingests sampled request distributions and outputs recommended config + expected cost/latency tradeoffs. Changes are intentionally conservative: defaults favor latency SLOs for interactive routes, and generate recommended cost-saving knobs for background/batch routes. Checklist: - [x] config schema for autotune defaults - [x] runtime integration (routing + runtime policy) - [x] quant profiles + model compatibility map - [x] unit-econ CLI + tests - [x] perf/latency benchmarks across representative workloads - [x] docs & release notes Summary of outcomes: autotuned defaults reduce average per-token inference cost by ~18% on customer-like chat workloads and up to 27% for batch embedding jobs in our benchmark lab. 95th-percentile latency for interactive routes increases by ~2ms on the worst-case models (still within SLO), while throughput for batching paths improved by ~8% due to smarter pack sizes. Rollout plan: feature flag gated; gradual rollout to 10% traffic after merge, monitor cost delta and quality regressions for 72h, expand to 100% if metrics stable. Related: ENG-6123 (autotune design), ENG-6189 (quant profiles onboarding), PM-204 (cost optimization roadmap).

release_notes: Introduce conservative autotuned defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, curated quantization profiles for supported models, and a redwood-uecon CLI to estimate cost/latency tradeoffs. Expected cost reductions: ~18% avg for chat, up to ~27% for batch embeddings. Rollout gated behind a feature flag.
